title: How Many Starting Points of a Circular Text Spell the Pattern?

concept.title: Unroll the circle by appending the first |p| - 1 letters of the text, then count the matches that start inside the original text
body: A text is written around a circle, so after its last letter comes its first letter again. For every starting letter of the circle, read `|p|` letters clockwise. Count the starting letters for which the word read is **equal to the pattern**. For the circular text `abcab` and the pattern `cab`, the five starts give `abc`, `bca`, `cab`, `aba` and `bab`, so only one start matches and the answer is 1.

A read of `|p|` letters that starts at the position `i` of the text and goes around the end is a substring of the text **written twice**. It is enough to append to the text its first `|p| - 1` letters: `u = t + t[0 .. |p| - 2]`. A match of `p` in `u` that starts at the position `i < |t|` corresponds to the start `i` on the circle (there are no matches that start at a position `>= |t|`, because there are only `|p| - 1` extra letters). So count the occurrences of `p` in `u` with the prefix function of `p + "#" + u`.

body.code:
u = t + t[:len(p) - 1]
c = p + "#" + u
pi = prefix_function(c)
m = len(p)
count = sum(1 for i in range(m + 1, len(c)) if pi[i] == m)
print(count)

body: Each start position of the circle is counted once, even if the pattern is as long as the text (then `u` has `|t| + |t| - 1` letters). For a text like `aaaa` and the pattern `aa` the answer is 4: every start gives `aa`. The program is linear in the size of the text.

statement: A circular text `t` and a pattern `p` (not longer than `t`) are given. For each of the `|t|` letters of the circle, read `|p|` letters starting from it and going around. Print how many of these reads are equal to `p`.
inputFormat: The first line has the circular text `t`.
The second line has the pattern `p`.
outputFormat: Print the number of starting letters.
constraints: 1 <= length of p <= length of t <= 40000
Both words consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.note: The five starts give abc, bca, cab, aba and bab; only the third matches: 1.

hints: Extend the text with its first |p| - 1 letters.
Count the occurrences of the pattern in the extended text.
Occurrences can only start inside the original text.

explanation: The text is extended with its first |p| - 1 letters and the occurrences of the pattern in the extended text are counted with the prefix function; every occurrence starts inside the original text.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def prefix_function(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        k = pi[i - 1]
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    return pi

t = input().strip()
p = input().strip()

m = len(p)
u = t + t[:m - 1]
c = p + "#" + u
pi = prefix_function(c)
print(sum(1 for i in range(m + 1, len(c)) if pi[i] == m))
